Algonquian indians have a term for this called Wetiko or Wendigo. In myth the Wetiko is a cannibalistic man-eating monster or person who becomes such a monster--or is possessed by its spirit--by succumbing to greed, gluttony, selfishness, or avarice. The term was adopted by psychologists to refer to people with a delusional compulsion toward cannibalism or thoughts and fears about it. But the natives had another meaning for this. They saw it also as a social/spiritual disease or contagious sociopathy that could spread through a society that lost its sense of empathy and communal responsibility. They would say all white people were wetiko because they almost universally exhibited this cannibalistic mentality. For them cannibalism meant more than just a flesh-eating compulsion. It was, figuratively, about a compulsion to consume life, all forms of it, around oneself. And in this sense the term has been adopted by some contemporary intellectuals. (inspired in particular by activist writer Jack D. Forbes) We now hear the term 'wetiko virus' or 'wetiko capitalism' to refer to a kind of memetic malaise of the present age and dominant culture. That seems very apt to me.
